NWSL Championship: Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current face off Saturday for the title

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL.
  • It has been revealed that the Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events.
  • Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was declared back in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

It has been revealed that the Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was declared back in June.

The Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the significant game:.

According to recent reports, date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

Industry observers note that the Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals rapidly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and newly introduced signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit swiftly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman remarked of the relationship with her teammates.

Industry observers note that "I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but promptly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

"I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper said.

"I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she said.

The Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • Recent findings suggest that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

Recent findings suggest that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

It has been revealed that previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the fresh format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

No. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

As noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, noted in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada said.

#71359. 2023 March Madness: Will UConn or San Diego State triumph in the national championship game that 'means everything?'

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (595 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

2023 March Madness: Will UConn or San Diego State triumph in the national championship game that 'means everything?'

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The University of Connecticut won its fifth men’s basketball national title with a 76-59 victory over San Diego State University on Monday night at NRG Stadium in Houston.
  • Senior guard Tristen Newton led UConn (31-8) with 19 points and 10 rebounds while Final Four Most Outstanding Player Adama Sanogo, a junior forward, chipped in with 17 points and 10 rebounds.
  • Industry observers note that “We weren’t ranked going into the year so we had the chip on our shoulder,” UConn head coach Dan Hurley told game broadcaster CBS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The University of Connecticut won its fifth men’s basketball national title with a 76-59 victory over San Diego State University on Monday night at NRG Stadium in Houston.

Senior guard Tristen Newton led UConn (31-8) with 19 points and 10 rebounds while Final Four Most Outstanding Player Adama Sanogo, a junior forward, chipped in with 17 points and 10 rebounds.

Industry observers note that “We weren’t ranked going into the year so we had the chip on our shoulder,” UConn head coach Dan Hurley told game broadcaster CBS. “We knew the level that we could play at, even through those dark times,” he added, referencing the team’s six losses in eight games during the regular season.

He stated going into the tournament his group had confidence garnered during the season.

“And when you have the type of leaders like Andre Jackson (game-high six assists Monday) and Adama Sanogo, they kept this team together, got us back on track and we knew we were the best team in the tournament going in and we just had to play to our level,” he added.

San Diego State (32-7) was topped by Keshad Johnson who had 14 points.

Sources indicate that UConn trailed very early but San Diego State was undone by an 11-minute, eight-second stretch in which they scored just five free throws and missed 12 consecutive shots from the field. The Huskies went from down 10-6 to up 36-24 at halftime.

The Aztecs made a run midway through the second half and narrowed the deficit to five at 60-55 with 5:19 to play but the Huskies scored the next nine to take a comfortable lead into the final two minutes.

It has been revealed that “We battled. Battled back to five in the second half, but gave them too much separation,” San Diego State coach Brian Dutcher said. “We had to be at our best. We weren’t at our best. A lot had to do with UConn.”.

Senior guard Adam Seiko told reporters they gave themselves a chance with their second half comeback but UConn “just made a little bit more plays” at the end.

Industry observers note that “They have a lot of weapons. They were pretty good,” mentioned Matt Bradley, also a senior guard. “To beat them, we had to make shots. I shot poorly. And you had to have a really good game to beat those dudes on the offensive end.”.

UConn won each of its six tournament games by at least 10 points, with its closest game being a 13-point win over the University of Miami in the national semifinals.

Recent findings suggest that “I just want to thank my teammates, my coaches who believed in me. If it were not for them I would not be here right now,” Sanogo told CBS.

Jordan Hawkins, who scored 16 points for UConn, talked about winning the crown one day after his cousin, Angel Reese of Louisiana State University, won the women’s title.

“I mean it’s absolutely amazing that we both get this opportunity and I mean the family reunion is going to be great so that’s all I know,” he stated.

Sources indicate that UConn enters rarefied air as only the sixth team to win five NCAA men’s basketball championships, joining UCLA (11), Kentucky (eight), North Carolina (six), Duke (five) and Indiana (five). All of UConn’s titles have come since 1999 with the most recent before Monday occurring in 2014.

UConn’s women’s teams have won 11 basketball national titles.

CNN’s Steve Almasy and Issy Ronald contributed to this report.

Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.

That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.

In the aftermath of that match, Ronaldo's mother Dolores released a furious and unprompted attack on the national team, claiming the defeat was just, and added she was happy to see the result.

Despite an emotional and historic tribute to Ronaldo pre-game, Dolores also expressed her unhappiness at what had unfolded, before she claimed the veteran's former international team-mates failed to show him the respect he deserved during his career.

Dolores has not always been an outspoken presence over the years, but has often stepped up to defend her son when she feels necessary.

So, in light of her outburst, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at other examples of when the mums of footballers have got involved in their careers.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum became embroiled in her son's row with Portugal's national team after saying she was happy to see them suffer a heavy defeat (Source: Instagram/doloresaveiroofficial).

Veronique Rabiot – Adrien Rabiot.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique has developed a reputation as an uncompromising and fiercely protective negotiator in her role as his agent.

This has seen the French midfielder face several flashpoints in his career, beginning  when Veronique pulled him out of Man City's academy after just six months in 2008 because she felt they were not looking after his interests like they should be.

During his time at PSG, where Rabiot ultimately broke through and spent seven seasons in the first team, Veronique then frequently clashed with the club's hierarchy.

Potential transfers to Roma and Man United during his career have also both collapsed late on, a factor some reports attach to Veronique's role in the deals.

There have been several notable flashpoints on the international stage too, not least when she backed her son's controversial decision to withdraw from France's standby list for the 2018 World Cup.

But that was nothing compared to the aftermath of France's shock exit from Euro 2020 at the last-16 stage.

Veronique made headlines at the time for engaging in a heated confrontation with the parents of Kylian Mbappe and the entourage of Paul Pogba in the stands over on-pitch errors and perceived arrogance during Les Bleus' campaign.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique (centre) has developed a reputation as a formidable force.

As the mother of one of the best footballers on the planet, Fayza Lamari was always likely to be a major powerbroker, and she has played a key role in Kylian Mbappe's career, acting as his chief negotiator and business manager.

This has seen Fayza oversee Mbappe's commercial obligations and image rights, while she played a central role in his dramatic contract extension at PSG in 2022.

Sources indicate that she was similarly important when Mbappe joined Real Madrid in 2024. On that occasion, she was credited for helping to secure a huge signing bonus and favourable image rights split for her son.

Fayza hasn't been afraid to publicly stand up for the forward, and she was key in the legal dispute over unpaid salary and bonuses that he felt he was owed by PSG after his exit.

PSG were ultimately ordered to pay Mbappe €60million (£52.5m) by a French court in a major victory for Fayza.

Kylian Mbappe's mum Fayza (also pictured with his brother Ethan) has played a key role in the commercial side of his career.

Sheila Ebana has been a foundational and supportive presence throughout Lamine Yamal's childhood and rise into professional football.

But, alongside regularly attending Yamal's games, Sheila has become a celebrity in her own right after embracing her public profile.

She regularly provides an insight into her life and shares behind the scenes clips with Yamal and his half brother Keyne on social media, racking up 2.8million followers on Instagram and 2.6million on TikTok.

Sheila has also regularly made paid appearances and attended VIP events, including a bizarre Christmas gala dinner that Daily Mail Sport went to in November 2025 where members of the public paid hundreds of pounds for a three-course meal, champagne, entertainment and a meet-and-greet.

To demonstrate how Sheila has embraced her fame, she once responded to online critics by retorting: 'I don't just think I'm famous - I am.'.

Lamine Yamal's mum (pictured below together with his half-brother Keyne) has embraced her celebrity fame.

Denise Bellingham – Jude Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham has often credited his mother Denise for helping to manage his life off the pitch and keep him grounded.

When he moved to Germany to join Borussia Dortmund as a 17-year-old, Denise went with him – before subsequently following the midfielder to Spain after his transfer to Real Madrid – while his father Mark stayed with his brother Jobe.

She is understood to handle his domestic affairs and finances, while Bellingham inadvertently revealed during the 2022 World Cup that she still made his bed.

Denise has generally provided a constant source of advice, logistical support – which has included driving him to training in the past – and organisational help throughout his time in the game.

The England star is clearly appreciative of all she has done, describing her as his 'queen' and 'backbone', and crediting her with helping to keep him level headed throughout the highs and lows of his career.

Jude Bellingham (pictured also with dad Mark and brother Jobe) has described his mum Denise as his 'queen' and 'backbone'.

Marcia Lewis – Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mother Marcia Lewis has played a crucial role in his rise into Arsenal and England's first team.

When Lewis-Skelly entered the Arsenal academy system at the age of eight, Marcia wanted to learn more about football to ensure she could protect and guide her son's progression.

She subsequently qualified as an agent, meaning she now represents Lewis-Skelly, and also enrolled in a Master's degree in Football Business.

Marcia has since taken part in contract negotiations and filtered external pressures away from her son during his development.

She was later inspired to set up the No1Fan.club, a platform that aims to support families who have children in academy football.

The outlet is dedicated to helping navigate various challenges that arise, such as dealing with scouts, agents and the general pressures associated with youth football.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mum Marcia Lewis tried to learn more about the business of football so she would be able to support her son on his journey (Source: Instagram/myleslewisskelly).

Harry Maguire's mother Zoe has taken a more low-profile approach to her son's career than others, yet she has never been afraid to speak out when she feels the need to.

This included back in 2023 when she snapped after years of watching her son face significant abuse, both online and in stadiums.

At the time, Zoe labelled the heat on the defender as 'disgraceful' and 'unacceptable', and noted it went 'far beyond' football.

She re-emerged into the public eye three years later when Maguire was snubbed from England's World Cup squad.

After that, she tweeted: 'Absolutely disgusted.'.

In another post addressing Maguire, she added: 'You couldn’t have done anymore. Hold your head high …Disgraceful.'.

Industry News: Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized strategy is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it.
  • In a recent development, rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise.
  • LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized strategy is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

In a recent development, rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

Recent findings suggest that "I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she remarked Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

Industry observers note that "I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

Sources indicate that "She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan noted, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

Industry observers note that "I am excited to go in every day," Morgan mentioned. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

"We have these massive red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

"I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman mentioned. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many upcoming players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

Industry observers note that "Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone mentioned. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

In a recent development, before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly crucial for us to keep Trinity in this league," she remarked. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

"She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] New York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

Industry observers note that "She's fun, she's engaging," Stone remarked. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

It has been revealed that rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

Industry observers note that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone mentioned. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

Borussia Dortmundâs brand-new away kit for the 2025/26 season has sparked fury among supporters, prompting the club to acknowledge the backlash and vow to respond.

The kit, which combines a white base with black sleeves and neon yellow detailing, was worn for the first time in Saturdayâs 2-0 Bundesliga win over Heidenheim.

But instead of excitement, its debut was met with anger in the stands and online. Fans unfurled banners blasting it as âthe cruelest jersey in the leagueâ while chants of âWe want black and yellow jerseysâ rang out before kick-off, a pointed reminder of the clubâs traditional colours.

Club bosses have now pledged to listen.

Sources indicate that managing director Carsten Cramer took personal responsibility for the fallout, telling reporters: "The criticism has been received, and we are addressing it. The responsibility lies with me. We won't always be able to please everyone when selecting jerseys.".

Sporting director Sebastian Kehl was more measured, reminding fans that opinions on kit design are always split.

It has been revealed that "I think we have different opinions about jerseys every year," he remarked. "It will never be the case that a Borussia Dortmund jersey meets with 100 percent approval. Fundamentally, we know which colors represent our city and our club, and that this is reflected in the design of almost all jerseys.".

He added, with a touch of humour: "However, there are also people who want something younger, something fresh, something creative. The upcoming jersey brought BVB three points in Heidenheim. A successful jersey, I'd say. Everything else is a discussion that we as a club consider normal.".

Emery endures heaviest European defeat as Villa manager to old foes Barcelona

💡 Key Takeaways
  • While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.
  • His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.
  • Recent findings suggest that it was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

Recent findings suggest that it was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

This latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.

Aston Villa make a mistake at the back and Lamine Yamal makes them pay inside 10 minutes ⚡ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1IcWOPMJlt.

It has been revealed that at the heart of Barcelona’s victory was Lamine Yamal, their outstanding jewel from the academy. The 19-year-old became the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, eclipsing the record of 13 he previously shared with Kylian Mbappé, with the opening goal.

Yamal was orchestrating everything from the pace of the match to the volume of the supporters, at one point imploring them to raise the noise in the first half with both arms aloft.

There was also another impressive performance from England international Anthony Gordon and Raphinha, who dedicated his two goals to the memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife forward, who died on Tuesday.

With that tragedy fresh in the minds and the Nou Camp under construction, it was a peculiar atmosphere at times.

The defeat marked the end of Villa’s 100 per cent record in the competition, with a tough test away at Galatasaray up next before they host PSG in December. They remain high up in the table and have often displayed a propensity to bounce back rapidly from defeats.

Emery mentioned: “We are in a process and this was a very good test against a team like Barcelona. We are not at the level we want to achieve but there are a lot of experiences for us to take. Overall, we are competing fantastically in the Champions League and there is still work to do.

“Over the process we’ve had here, we have made mistakes but then overcame them. We accept this defeat but take a lot of information from it.”.

Nine years have passed since Emery’s last visit in this competition and time has not proved a great healer.

Sources indicate that then in charge of PSG, Emery witnessed his team surrender a 4-0 first-leg lead to lose 6-5 on aggregate. Any matches where he is involved at the Nou Camp will revive memories of that remarkable comeback. He must have feared a repeat of more pain when Yamal, making his 37th Champions League appearance, rewarded Barcelona’s early pressure.

Villa’s defending needed to be as close to perfect as possible, but they were exposed after a poor error of judgment from Gomes. Under pressure from Barcelona’s attackers, Gomes panicked and played a blind pass into the path of Yamal, who bent his left-footed shot into the corner.

Recent findings suggest that that mistake could have threatened to damage confidence but Villa did respond. Matty Cash’s half-volley from inside the penalty area was only a few inches wide, while Johan Manzambi side-footed wide of the goal after a quick break down the right from Nicolas Jackson.

With Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart and Jules Koundé all absent here, Barcelona’s defence did appear vulnerable. Jackson was targeting the flanks and having his more dangerous moments challenging their high line. Emery paced his technical area, imploring his players to remain focused.

In a recent development, aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

In a recent development, aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

Sources indicate that “In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery stated. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

It has been revealed that barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick stated. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which demonstrated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.
  • At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.

At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.

According to recent reports, although probably unrelated, these incidents highlight a broader transformation in cybersecurity, say researchers. Artificial intelligence is changing how software vulnerabilities are discovered, allowing both attackers and security specialists to examine vast quantities of computer code at unprecedented speed.

“I think vulnerability discovery without AI is basically dead,” says Steven Murdoch, a computer security researcher at University College London. Researchers in the field who don’t use the technology now risk falling behind, he says.

Recent findings suggest that AI can find weaknesses in software much faster than humans can, giving attackers time to exploit vulnerabilities before organizations can fix them. Researchers now want to understand how thoroughly AI can check software for security flaws, and whether it could introduce new weaknesses.

Industry observers note that agentic systems help attackers identify security vulnerabilities more rapidly and systematically. While hackers previously had to spend hours inspecting websites and probing software for weaknesses that offered unauthorized access to networks, AI agents use automated tools that can search millions of lines of computer code.

Google has reported that attackers have already used agentic AI to examine software updates, identify the security problems they address, and then find ways to exploit them.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

“For me, it's about the scale,” says Daniel Gardham, a cybersecurity researcher at the University of Surrey. AI tends to find the same kinds of weaknesses as human hackers, but it makes it easier for people with limited technical expertise to break into systems.

“They can set an AI agent off and come back in 20 minutes and have dozens of results already,” he indicates.

Even with AI, most security breaches still involve human failure, he claims, such as weak passwords (a common problem with Europe’s supermarket freezers was that passwords were defaults such as ‘admin’ or ‘12345’) or clicking on links from unfamiliar sources. AI-crafted messages can make such phishing messages more convincing and so more likely to succeed. They can draw on publicly available information to personalize fraudulent communications and make them appear authentic.

Industry observers note that murdoch indicates AI is particularly good at discovering familiar kinds of software flaws, even if the most accomplished human researchers remain better at finding entirely new types of weakness. “They don't need to sleep,” he says. “You can happily work a hundred of them in parallel.”.

These capabilities of AI helped discover security flaws in Java and PHP software, two programming languages that build cross-platform software and websites. In the Java case, for example, AI identified circumstances that could allow an attacker to corrupt computer memory. But Murdoch indicates the significance of the issue has been exaggerated.

The Java vulnerability, he states: “Is a real problem, but it’s not one of the top ten vulnerabilities this year or probably even this week.”.

Just like hackers, cybersecurity researchers are using AI tools to swiftly and efficiently find weaknesses in computer systems. Murdoch notes this has become increasingly notable to vulnerability researchers, who can now examine much larger quantities of software and work out how to patch up the defences where necessary. Researchers are also developing AI agents that can detect and repair vulnerabilities automatically.

When security researchers uncover a weakness, they typically notify the software developer privately, allowing engineers to prepare a remedy before publishing details of the problem.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

Murdoch says the use of AI in cyber security has shortened the time window between public disclosure and attempted exploitation – from several weeks, to just a few days.

Industry observers note that rushing an update can bring its own problems. A software patch can interfere with other programs and cause the sort of outage that organisations are trying to avoid.

“The life for the defenders who are trying to fix things has become significantly harder,” Murdoch states.

According to recent reports, it’s unlikely that the recent tech outages were connected as large-scale cyber-attack, says Murdoch. The most prominent disruptions, he says, are likely technical malfunctions rather than anything more sinister.

Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • Sources indicate that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

Sources indicate that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

The first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

At that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, said additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

Recent findings suggest that "Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler said. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

Industry observers note that "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," remarked Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

Industry observers note that LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," remarked BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

Recent findings suggest that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," remarked Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," said Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

Manchester City have been dealt a multi-billion-pound blow, following their guilty verdict over breaching Premier League rules.

In September, an independent panel ruled that Man City were guilty of over 100 charges of breaking financial rules, with the Premier League confirming the verdict in an official statement.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, described the case as “the most significant in Premier League history”, with the league's own statement using the word “sham” five times.

While the Sky Blues face uncertainty on the pitch – including whether or not they will be relegated from the Premier League as a result of a points deduction – there has reportedly been an impact behind the scenes, too.

The Financial Times reports that United States-based investment firm Apollo Global Management have abandoned a $2 billion loan to City owner Sheikh Mansour – worth just over £1.5bn – following the Premier League's verdict.

Talks were ongoing over the arrangement between The City Football Group and the private capital group, who manage more than $1 trillion of assets and have already dealt with the likes of Atletico Madrid and Nottingham Forest previously.

According to the report, “The loan from Apollo would have provided the group, which also owns clubs in Europe, the Americas and Asia, with extra liquidity as well as being used to refinance existing credit facilities, according to people familiar with the matter.”.

City are yet to feel the effects of the Premier League's verdict but have lost the last three matches in the Premier League after opening the season with seven straight wins.

The six-time champions responded to the news of the verdict with an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield earlier this season, with the Anfield faithful bringing banners calling out their opponents.

Leading stars such as Erling Haaland, meanwhile, have been questioned over their futures, while former Citizens Manuel Akanji and Kyle Walker have both expressed worry that their titles could be revoked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The international break is over, and it's now time to get back to the usual business with European soccer resuming alongside the MLS playoffs in the United States. It was supposed to be a quiet break, but that wasn't the case at all, since Manchester United decided to part ways with Michael Carrick and appointed Mauricio Pochettino, who had recently signed a new deal with the United States men's national team but decided to leave after the break. Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid will battle with Barcelona for the LaLiga title, while Como are still one of the most interesting sides to watch in the near future. Let's now take a look at the five teams to watch after the break, starting with the Red Devils.

Sources indicate that the biggest change of the break: Manchester United sacked coach and club legend Michael Carrick and replaced him with Pochettino, who makes his Premier League comeback after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. As the English giants are currently sitting 18th in the standings, this is a major task for the now-former USMNT head coach, who will make his return at Anfield against Liverpool in his opening game at United. It's a daunting start in one of the most hostile atmospheres in the country. For Pochettino, the challenge will be to strike the right balance between delivering short-term results and laying the foundations for a newly introduced chapter at the club. His ambition will be to usher in a fresh cycle at an institution that has endured one crisis after another since Sir Alex Ferguson stepped down more than a decade ago.

Speaking of a former Manchester United head coach, Jose Mourinho has had some ups and downs early in his first season back at Real Madrid. After winning an exciting away El Clasico match against Barcelona, Mourinho's team is only three points behind Hansi Flick's side right now and is eyeing the possibility of challenging them for the LaLiga title this season. They certainly have all the ingredients to make it happen, particularly following some remarkable additions to the squad in the summer of 2026. Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are arguably entering their prime and appear ready to take the team to the next level, supported by a number of exciting young prospects who could play a key role in shaping the club's future. Will Mourinho be able to win a trophy in his first season back at the club? That would be a story.

According to recent reports, if there is one team to watch in Serie A, it's Como. The side led by Cesc Fabregas is impressing both domestically and in Europe, as it is at the moment fourth in the league-phase standings of the UEFA Champions League. Fabregas can count on some of the best players in the league, such as Nico Paz, the Argentine talent who is now also expected to lead the national team after Lionel Messi's retirement. The question is how far Como can go this season, given that playing every three days can be a big challenge for players who have never experienced it. They may still have to pay the price in the league, but qualifying for at least the playoffs of Europe's elite competition would remain a realistic target and, given the circumstances, a remarkable achievement in itself.

Industry observers note that it's always about Manchester City: the Citizens are still waiting to learn what sanctions they will face after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. They are facing a challenging season that might have an impact on the years ahead. It's not clear what the sanctions will be, but we will likely know more before the end of the current season. On the pitch, they are also facing a season of changes as longtime coach Pep Guardiola left the club in the summer and was replaced by Enzo Maresca, who is now overseeing that transition.

Industry observers note that spanish soccer is not just about Real Madrid and Barcelona: Atletico Madrid are once again near the top of the standings, five points behind the Blaugrana. Diego Simeone, who has coached the club since 2011, is an Atletico Madrid legend who has faced so many changes over the years but has always been able to recreate the right atmosphere and environment to succeed. Atletico have changed their tactical approach and playing style many times, but they are still near the top, and that is what makes Simeone special.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk stated on Friday that the company would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur stated Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk stated on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

Unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding issues meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the company sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

For orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

The IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest organization was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a company focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the firm's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

According to recent reports, starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in recent years, Louisville City FC have been one of the most successful regular-season teams in United Soccer League history, but it hasn't translated to winning the big game. They haven't won the USL Championship since 2018, and while this season has been a trying time dealing with injuries and a latest coach taking over, they're playing their best soccer when it matters to set up a strange clash with Sacramento Republic at noon Eastern on Saturday. What's strange isn't that it's Louisville and Sacramento meeting, but that the match kicks off at 9 a.m. local time, a time Louisville forward Ray Serrano says he hasn't played soccer at since he was 15. While it's a regular training time for Louisville and they'll try to keep things on an East Coast timeline, it's hard not to take the shift into account when planning for a final.

It's a challenge that comes with the desire to reach as many fans as possible with a final of this magnitude. Leagues have to work with broadcast networks to ensure that the slots work, and for the USL, having the game on CBS is worth the risk of a 9 a.m. local start with a West Coast team hosting. It's nothing Louisville won't be prepared for, as they look to keep their internal clocks on Eastern Standard Time.

It has been revealed that "No, we're trying to stay on Eastern Time, so for us, it's training time," defender Kyle Adams said. "Wake up at 8:00 a.m., but really it's 5:00 a.m. Go to sleep a little bit earlier. Try to do everything really just to stay on Eastern Time, eat a little bit earlier on the night before, and just treat it as going into training, and then get after them.".

It has been revealed that other teams have dealt with similar challenges, like the Los Angeles Rams when playing an NFL game in Australia, but it's still a struggle to deal with en route to a cup final as Louisville look to reach the pinnacle of the sport for the first time since 2018. Winners of the Prinx Tires USL Cup during the regular season, they do have cup experience that will prove to be fruitful in this competition, which Adams noted has been something that brings the injury-riddled squad together. "We know in the last few years we've struggled in these knockout games, but this year we've turned it on," Serrano said. "It has been really good preparation, just the mentality of going into them, how we deal with the pressure, and we're seeing the fruits of all that now.".

It's cliche to say that because of the adversity that they've dealt with, the club is playing its best soccer when it matters, but between using four goalkeepers during the season and seeing manager Danny Cruz depart to be an assistant manager with Minnesota United, it hasn't been an easy task for interim manager Simon Bird to get this team on the right track at this critical juncture.

"Going back to the main part is the adversity that we've faced. You mentioned injuries, having to deal with that side of it, some of the various parts of the season, different things we've had to deal with from a tactical or technical standpoint, where we've lost games, and we feel that we shouldn't have lost games," Bird noted when reflecting on the team's development under his leadership. "The most impressive thing I said to the guys today, yesterday in training, we worked on our defensive structure, but the whole training session I thought was excellent, not just the defensive side, off the ball but with the ball, and to see it all come together towards the end of the season is really rewarding. Hopefully, we can carry that on and put together a complete performance, and that's what we've had throughout the season-moments where we've let ourselves down in all these different areas, set pieces, maybe transition at other times, in front of goal. So, putting it all together for a complete performance on Saturday is the goal.".

Traveling away to a tough environment in Heart Health Park, Louisville will meet the hottest team in the league in Sacramento Republic. They've ridden a club-record 16-game unbeaten run to the final based on their defense. That has set a strong foundation to build on, and it could make the final one where the first team to score a goal wins the match. Sacramento's squad also has experience in USL Cup finals, which goes a long way when preparing for games of this stature.

Industry observers note that "I don't think it can hurt to have that. This would be a step forward for my first final. I think experience is invaluable for players and for staff," Sacramento coach Neil Collins noted. "But then there's also the recognition that every game is different, every team is different, and every season is different. So it's just trying to get the balance right and enjoy the opportunity. You've got to have the mechanisms to control the things you can control. Obviously, the opposition team is trying to do the same, and we've got to do everything we can to be ready to take the opportunity when it comes. But the experience will definitely help us; there's plenty of that in our dressing room.".

Sources indicate that it's a final where the best that the league has to offer will be on display, and it couldn't come at a better time. The summer of soccer, with the United States hosting the World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada, has truly turned into a soccer avalanche, and this final showcases one of the top atmospheres in the league. You can't ask for much better than that, as no matter what, a drought will come to an end. Sacramento Republic haven't won the final since 2014, while Louisville haven't won since 2018, and for these clubs, it will mean a lot to get back to the top.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone.
  • Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, right now above Juventus and Napoli in the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By FABRIZIO FERRARI FOR DAILY MAIL SPORT.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.

According to recent reports, not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, right now above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is Upcoming York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

Industry observers note that A month later a fresh sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

By the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday.

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October.

Much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

Sources indicate that he and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his upcoming passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

Notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

Industry observers note that frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

Then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

Whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season.

When it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how quickly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

Recent findings suggest that still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

Alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

It has been revealed that those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

Frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.
