Leeds expose Chelsea's unresolved defensive problems as Xabi Alonso's crew yet to find footing

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form.
  • Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea.
  • Sources indicate that and Alonso has tried a lot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form. In this most in-flux of Premier League seasons, Xabi Alonso still might leave her with something. It is not going to take particular excellence for a club like this to achieve the bare minimum of Champions League qualification. Adequacy might do it.

Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea. This 4-1 defeat at home to old rivals Leeds has them squeezed into the Premier League's middle ground, those above them very visible proof of how much more can be done with less. There is nothing false about that position. Since the last weeks of summer, Alonso's team have given up so much at the back that their likeliest route to success seemed to be supernova seasons from all three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Nothing else would paper over the cracks in the defense.

Sources indicate that and Alonso has tried a lot. Right backs in midfield, center backs as nominal left wing backs that are actually auxiliary central midfielders, switching the right wing back to center forward: in isolation, you could make a case for so many of these adjustments. When the performances are so inconsistent, why not change the XI every game? Alonso's success at Bayer Leverkusen, coupled with the inquisitive footballing mind that made the player so beloved of elite coaches, have earned him the right to experiment.

Every change, however, begs the question of what the foundations underlying all this are. Those ought to have shone through this afternoon. Alonso's was as straightforward an XI as he has named. Estevao, Palmer and Rogers off an orthodox center forward, Moises Caicedo running the double pivot and an orthodox back four in front of Emiliano Martinez. This looked like a team intent on playing its way.

Instead, they had Leeds' game foisted upon them. That might have been different if they had not lost Caicedo. He seemed to have a handle on the game before colliding with James Justin as both competed for a high ball. Those often seemed like the only sort up for grabs today; even when Chelsea played well, they were playing the sort of game Leeds wanted. This wasn't quite the rapid attacking up the gut with which Xabi Alonso charmed the Premier League early in this season. It was bypass the press-ball, get it straight up to the final third and see what comes of it.

It can work. Justin, exemplary as a man-marker without the ball and roving agent of chaos in the Chelsea half, cleared a goal kick straight into the back of Morgan Rogers. He moved swiftly up the Leeds gut, his pass to Emmanuel Emegha delivered at just the right moment for the Premier League debutant to slam in the opener. It was perhaps the only moment of clinical execution from the Blues.

According to recent reports, they needed so many more. After all, this is a team that fails to meet the standards in so many aspects of defending. They press like a newly promoted team. They always seem to name one defender who can be picked on in the duels (starting left back Pep Charravia ranks 101st of 102 defenders for duel success over 300-plus Premier League minutes). Midfielders routinely abandon runners. When Caicedo left this game the feint thread holding the team together was cut.

Sources indicate that no one had the composure to deal with the bouncing ball moments after Emegha's opener, Noah Okafor free to move into the box and shoot low through a crowd of legs. No one seemed truly live to the danger for Okafor's second, thundered into the roof of the net when Chelsea could not repel pressure down their right. Between that a contentious penalty, Jayden Bogle's long-range effort striking Rogers right in the grey area between sleeve and arm. If that hadn't been the moment when Chelsea caved, another would have come along.

Recent findings suggest that "Leeds believed more than us," Alonso admitted. "We didn't show a good enough reaction." The quick one-two punch had been more than enough to send Chelsea heads to the floor.

According to recent reports, A two-goal deficit ought not to be beyond their reach, but the final 32 minutes saw them outshot seven to six with fewer passes completed into the penalty area. Palmer's most notable action of this game was to row with Joao Pedro as he made his way down the tunnel. Nothing he could have done would have overcome the problems Chelsea made for themselves at the other end. It really wouldn't hurt, though if he did more than nothing.

These feel like problems unresolved by a manager who was supposed to be the savior. Eleven Premier League games is not a lot to turn the tide but it is enough to give us a sense of who this team are. The answer is a team whose early scoring streak covered for a below-average attack (1.25 non-penalty expected goals per game, 14th in the Premier League) and a below-average defense (1.44 non-penalty expected goals allowed per game, 15th in the Premier League). The game state-warping impact of scoring with your first shot can only mitigate so much.

It has been revealed that is it time for a conversation about Alonso and pressure? If so it has to be caveated by the unity and purpose he fostered at Bayer Leverkusen, qualities this dressing room sorely needs. He might not have corralled the superstars at Real Madrid but the press and possession system he forged could have achieved great things given time. Stitching together a version of this Chelsea, overloaded with number 10s and underpowered defensive players, that suits the more direct and chaotic Premier League was always going to be a coaching challenge.

Industry observers note that and of course this is not the Roman Abramovich era. Swapping out coaches is not a silver bullet for perennial trophy contenders but instead the modus operandi of an ownership group that are the most serious problem at Stamford Bridge. Someone is going to have to be afforded time to corral this squad or indeed tear it down and start again. Doing that is going to be a club-wide effort, including fans. Few of them hung around to wave off a side who had allowed old rivals Leeds a first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, the same side who had let Tottenham break the habit of a lifetime last month.

The vibes are bad. The performances might be worse. This brand latest start is feeling all too familiar.

#71294. Tech Report: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1282 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other.
  • "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years.
  • Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation, told DW.

"Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner stated Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

Critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This upcoming exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

"I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's notable to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner remarked. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher indicates 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that for today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning.".

Sources indicate that A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

In a recent development, the next step, Wagner mentioned, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

In a recent development, "For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he mentioned.

Eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

Sources indicate that in November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

Her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

Her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

In a recent development, her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

It has been revealed that eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she said. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?".

Industry observers note that it wasn't until much later that she first spoke publicly about the horrors of her early childhood. In 2011, she delivered a commemorative speech in Auschwitz on the anniversary of the camp's liberation. Since 2025, she has served as chair of the International Auschwitz Committee. A heart attack in 2014 motivated her to write her first book. "I was in intensive care. I thought to myself: If I get out of here healthy, I'll write a book.".

Her memoir, "The Number on Your Forearm is Blue Like Your Eyes," was first released in 2016. The English translation followed in 2024. Since its publication, hardly a day has passed without someone asking Eva Umlauf to share her story.

She is appalled by the disrespectful behavior of young people at former concentration camps and by growing ignorance about the Holocaust. Sometimes, people even ask if she's too old to have a tattoo. But she also recalls a young man on the Munich subway who noticed the number on her arm and told her: "I want to apologize to you for what my ancestors did to you.".

According to recent reports, umlauf never imagined that antisemitism would once again become so widespread in Europe and the United States. Nor did she expect the rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

"I go into schools. I'm so overwhelmed by the number of requests asking for my availability. And yet, the AfD is growing faster than I can reach students. It makes me think all this work is for nothing," she told DW.

According to recent reports, germany must never again fall under a right-wing dictatorship, she stressed. "'Never again' sounds nice, but all I can say is: It's happening again! Wouldn't 'Here We Go Again: Never Again' make a good title for the exhibition?".

She also shared her message to young people in the exhibition catalog, "Never Again": "You are not responsible for the crimes of your grandparents and great-grandparents. But you are responsible for the future. […] You are the generation that will shape our world. Make it a place where everyone can grow up safely, regardless of their background, faith or skin color.".

In a recent development, she continues: "You don't have to be perfect. You just have to stay alert. Take care of your country.".

The exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in the Bundeskunsthalle in Bonn runs through May 2, 2027.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Sources indicate that good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

Tuchel’s only major injury doubt from the last squad are Arsenal’s Bukao Saka and Como’s Trevoh Chalobah as well as the more long-term absentee Tino Livramento, the man Chalobah replaced in the World Cup 26. For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

Whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant matter of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Edwin van der Sar has his wife to thank for promptly spotting the symptoms when he suffered a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

The former Ajax, Juventus, Fulham and Manchester United great has since gone on to make a full recovery, and appeared for an Ajax Legends side against their Barcelona counterparts at the Johan Cruyff Arena last weekend.

But at the time it happened, Van der Sar's wife, Annemarie van Kesteren, knew exactly what was happening having suffered a brain haemorrhage herself back in 2009.

Van der Sar told FourFourTwo: "Annemarie knew what was happening. I had this strange feeling that something wasn't right.

"Then before you know it, you see the light and the light hurts your eyes. I had pain in my head.

"From that point onwards, you just let yourself go, and hope the ambulance and the people around you take care of you.

"You have to put your faith, your life, into the hands of people who are trained for that and who specialise in it.".

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a way, Van der Sar considers the timing to be fortuitous: he had only recent resigned as Ajax chief executive after seven years in the post.

He noted: "I'd stepped away five or six weeks before [from Ajax], so I had all the time in the world to recover, rest and get better.

"If I'd still had the job, I think the eagerness and the demands of the position might have made my recovery harder.

"When you're responsible for a club, a organization or an organisation, you want to be there.

"Luckily, I had no ties and nothing else to focus on apart from myself and my recovery. I've had a few chats - but nothing has really felt right.

"I'm enjoying my life at the moment, and I'm not actively looking for another position.".

It has been revealed that for the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions. Republic defeated Louisville City FC in a penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw Saturday at Heart Health Park, capturing the club's second title and extending its unbeaten run to 17 matches.

In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.

RYAN SPAULDING HAS WON THE USL CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE FOR @SacRepublicFC‼️😤#USLonCBS | @bestwestern pic.twitter.com/OeFARGXyyh.

Sources indicate that the second star comes at a symbolic moment for Sacramento Republic, which is preparing to move from Heart Health Park and into a latest 20,000-seat soccer-specific venue in the Railyards district of downtown Sacramento in 2028. The emotions were evident on the faces of Louisville City players after the loss as they came to terms with what happened.

Despite an early start to the USL Cup final in Sacramento, with kickoff at 9 a.m. local time, there was no need to wait for goals, as Louisville and Sacramento both scored within the opening 32 minutes. Cal Jennings struck in the 14th minute, while Ray Serrano answered in the 31st.

It was then the defenses that took the reins to calm the game down as Sacramento held possession to control a dangerous Louisville attack, and when Evan Davila's shootout attempt hit the post, it opened the door for Sacramento keeper Danny Vitiello to win it, and that he did.

An evenly matched final was exactly what many expected, and it delivered for Sacramento fans, who started tailgating at 5:30 a.m. and brought the energy from start to finish. Neil Collins' experienced side looked prepared for the moment, and had Mark-Anthony Kaye's effort not struck the post, Sacramento may have settled the match in regulation. Instead, it required a shootout, and that's where Republic ultimately got the job done.

On the Louisville side, despite winning the Prinx Tires Cup during the regular season, they've now failed to win the final in three appearances since their last triumph in 2018. Considering their regular-season success, they'll want to get over the hump, but given how consistent they've been, it's impossible to say they won't be back at this stage next season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.

McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

The result continues the teenager’s brilliant week after she broke the 400m freestyle world record last Tuesday – breaking defending Olympic champion Ariarne Titmus’ previous record of 3:56.40, which was set last May, in a time of 3:56.08.

Speaking after her latest triumph, McIntosh shared her emotions.

“That’s the first time I really vividly heard the crowd during my race,” McIntosh said, per Reuters.

“It’s amazing to have all my family and friends in the stands, cheering me on. It really helped me in the last 100 meters.”.

The Canadian teen made her Olympic debut aged 14 at Tokyo 2020, where she finished fourth in the 200-meter freestyle.

She bagged gold in the 200m butterfly and 400m medley at the world championships in 2022, as well as two golds at the Commonwealth Games in the 200m and 400m medleys.

She now trains in Florida under coach Brent Arckey with the Sarasota Sharks team.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) company.
  • The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.
  • The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) company.

The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US government officials drafted a memo about the allegations shortly before US President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping in May.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy has exposed him and the company to criticism that it may have allowed China to obtain valuable trade secrets as Beijing tries to gain an edge in the race to develop advanced AI models.

It has been revealed that nvidia is initiating an investigation led by independent board members and an external law firm. It mentioned in a statement that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.".

According to recent reports, "The board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," the tech giant said Sunday. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information.".

The company's shares fell in early trading on Monday.

While US intelligence officials have not commented publicly on the claims, Trump — with whom Jensen Huang has a close relationship — has backed the Nvidia boss.

Industry observers note that "He's an honorable guy," remarked Trump. "I have not spoken to him ​about it. I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine.".

Tim Culpan, an Asia tech reporter who has covered Nvidia and Huang closely for years, told DW that while Nvidia's fundamental strengths as a company remain in place, Huang is hugely personally damaged by the story.

"They're still going to make great chips and they're going to sell them to millions of customers around the world who want the best AI chips in the world," he noted.

"His opinion is going to carry a lot less weight now. And that, in the long term, will flow through to Nvidia and Nvidia's own corporate interests. So it won't be immediate. It's really a fact that he doesn't have the sway or the power that he might have had one week ago simply through this.".

Richard Windsor, a tech analyst and the founder of research company Radio Free Mobile, said the news could be very serious for Nvidia given how much the company has revolved around Huang for decades.

"This problem is particularly acute because Jensen Huang is very hands-on, meaning that the key decisions that led to its success were ultimately taken by him and because there is no obvious successor," he mentioned.

"I suspect we are about to find out just how much the market thinks that the company is dependent on its iconic founder and CEO.".

Nvidia and Huang's attitude toward China and potential Chinese customers has been a bone of contention with US intelligence officials — despite Huang's close relationship with Trump.

It has been revealed that huang has repeatedly lobbied Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. A 2025 export control deal heavily curbed sales, but Trump subsequently permitted the export of older H200 Nvidia chips to China in return for the US government receiving a cut of the sales.

However, that deal has been complicated and bogged down by Washington's strict export-license review. China has also initiated import controls, despite strong demand from Chinese companies. China lacks access to the most advanced AI-capable chips. Beijing wants to develop its own alternatives but has struggled to catch up.

Huang has argued that Chinese dependence on Nvidia's chips would prevent rivals such as Huawei from catching up and boosting China's ambitions to dominate AI supply chains.

However, that argument has been dismissed by many US intelligence officials. They fear that unlimited Chinese access to the most advanced Nvidia chips would boost China's domestic AI sector, lead to its AI models catching up with the leading US models and see the chips being used in Chinese military applications.

Recent findings suggest that the US-China rivalry has become a central theme in the global AI story, with both countries seeking to gain an upper hand in the technology. Leading US AI executives such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei have argued that US AI companies can't afford to take a prolonged pause to allow safety standards in AI to catch up, if they're going to prevent Chinese firms from gaining an advantage.

Washington's central fear over Huang's affair is that it could have led to Beijing obtaining vital trade secrets or other key information about how Nvidia makes its most advanced chips.

According to recent reports, windsor thinks Huang will survive the "severe test" due to his importance to the company. He also cast doubt on the extent to which Beijing and its leading tech firms have learned from Nvidia's chips, pointing to China's own chip ambitions and commitment to have its firms buy its own semiconductors.

"I am far from convinced that Chinese AI has materially benefited from technology or illicit chip imports that it gained from Nvidia," he stated.

The news comes at a particularly challenging moment for Nvidia, which has benefited massively from the AI boom thanks to its position as the leading maker of cutting-edge semiconductors needed for AI applications.

Nvidia's valuation has soared dramatically in recent years as companies rushed to buy its chips, becoming the world's first $5 trillion company in October 2025.

However, doubts over the sustainability of the $9 trillion capital expenditure AI boom have sparked a major sell-off in stocks related to the boom in recent weeks. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the US midterms have added to the doubts, given the strength of voter opposition to data center construction in the US.

Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • According to recent reports, diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

According to recent reports, diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old stated last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most notable players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another quickly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

According to recent reports, inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler remarked shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

Across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

According to recent reports, but who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

Industry observers note that in this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

According to recent reports, ‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer claims. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

Industry observers note that during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

In a recent development, spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another notable step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

Sources indicate that ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer says. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

Recent findings suggest that ‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

According to recent reports, the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

Sources indicate that ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he says. ‘He wants to achieve major things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

Daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there’s one thing Brighton and Hove Albion know how to do, it’s sell players for sizeable fees and replace them with bargain signings who prove to be just as good, if not better.

It has been revealed that they replaced Yves Bissouma with Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez with Bart Verbruggen, Leandro Trossard with Kaoru Mitoma, and Marc Cucurella with Pervis Estupinan. Even when Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister departed in the same summer, Brighton managed to maintain their upward trajectory thanks in part to the emergence of Carlos Baleba.

Now, having sold Baleba to Manchester United for £70 million, the Seagulls appear to have pulled off the same trick with another promising young midfielder: Chema Andres, who has developed a formidable partnership with veteran Pascal Gross in midfield.

Recent findings suggest that andres was still developing in Real Madrid’s academy less than two years ago. After honing his skills in the Spanish capital, he joined Stuttgart in 2025 for €3 million, where he quickly established himself as an important figure in midfield, steering them to a DFB-Pokal final and Champions League qualification.

He appeared destined to continue his development in Germany, but Brighton had other ideas. With just hours left in the summer transfer window, the Seagulls swooped in and signed him for £16 million. Fabian Hurzeler thrust him in at the deep end, and Andres quickly repaid his trust by assisting on his debut at Coventry and leading Brighton to an EFL Cup victory at Old Trafford.

A midfield masterclass from @BHAFC's Chema Andres 👏 https://t.co/9s4FUF7Kd2October 3, 2026.

In just his second season of senior football, Andres is emerging as one of the Premier League’s top midfielders. Brighton sit second in the table, five points behind Arsenal, one ahead of Manchester City and 14 clear of relegation-threatened Manchester United. At the heart of their start is Andres, whose defensive discipline and penetrative passing has made him indispensable after Baleba's departure.

While Baleba’s greatest strength lies in his ball-carrying ability, Andres offers Brighton a different route through opposition defenses. According to Gradient Sports, a football analysis tech giant, Andres is averaging 4.41 midfield line-breaking passes per 90 minutes, compared with Baleba’s 2.74 during his final season at Brighton. He is also completing 79.2% of these passes, well above Baleba’s 70.9%.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That superiority extends to more audacious, high-risk passes: Andres is attempting 2.02 attacking line-breaking passes per 90, nearly twice Baleba’s 1.05, while completing them with far greater accuracy (90.9% vs. 71.4%). Whereas Baleba relied on his explosive acceleration to bypass opponents, Andres is using his vision, composure and passing range to slice through defensive lines and find his teammates.

Recent findings suggest that andres is also making his presence felt off the ball. While he might not be the same all-action midfielder who thrives on charging around the pitch and throwing himself into duels, his positional awareness and anticipation have proved invaluable in shielding Brighton’s backline. No Premier League midfielder has registered more tackles per 90 (3.31) or blocks per 90 (2.94) than Andres this season, while his 64.7% success rate in 50/50 duels exceeds Baleba’s 62.5%.

It has been revealed that at 21 years-old, Andres is already imposing himself against the Premier League’s top sides. He excelled against Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice and found the back of the net in a 3–0 victory against defending champions Arsenal, before holding his own in a 1-0 win against Manchester City.

Despite costing Brighton less than a tenth of what City spent on Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez combined, Andrés helped the Seagulls secure their first away victory against City in 18 attempts, before playing a pivotal role in their hard-fought 2–0 win against Brentford.

For all his virtues, it would be premature to declare Andrés an outright upgrade on Baleba. Nevertheless, his passing intelligence, defensive anticipation and tactical discipline could make him an even better fit for Hurzeler’s system. Rather than simply replacing Baleba’s qualities, Brighton have found a midfielder whose strengths complement their style of play, once again demonstrating their knack for staying one step ahead of the transfer market.

According to recent reports, for a club that has built its reputation on unearthing hidden gems, molding them into stars, and selling them for astronomical profits, Andres is shaping up to be another transfer masterstroke. And if he can help Brighton secure a maiden Champions League qualification, Baleba’s departure might be remembered not as a setback, but as the catalyst for the greatest moment in the club’s history.

#71275. Tech Report: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1359 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1359 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border.
  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

"November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

It has been revealed that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how swiftly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

According to recent reports, the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

Recent findings suggest that today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

Industry observers note that at the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very quickly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

Meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

Industry observers note that in his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he stated, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an concern that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

Industry observers note that his photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he remarked.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

Sources indicate that according to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Sources indicate that streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she mentioned. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Industry observers note that interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

Industry observers note that the story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist stated she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

Industry observers note that in particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she noted. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

Could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, said Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

Industry observers note that "In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," stated Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical complications, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

"It's very vital to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," said Feuchtenberger.

"For me personally, the whole concern of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she noted. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

"This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," said Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

According to recent reports, cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, an ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy.
  • Sources indicate that the big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area.
  • According to recent reports, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, an ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy. Mikel Arteta’s instant simmering fury at being denied a first-half penalty may also have turned into something rather more explosive had Martin Odegaard not later sent the champions six points clear with a ninth win in 10 Premier League games.

Sources indicate that the big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area. Which came first? The intervention of VAR suggested the latter. But Hallam duly went to check the pitch-side monitor before then announcing the former.

According to recent reports, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared. Cue cheers from the home Arsenal crowd. “However…,” he went on. “Red No 29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City.”.

#ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

It all sounded so decisive that most inside the Emirates instinctively thought the outcome reasonable. But then came a closer look at the rules. And Law 11.2 certainly did seem to support Arteta’s protestations: “In situations where a player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

Arteta clearly saw no value after the match in aiming much criticism at Hallam following a fourth 1-0 win in 10 league games, but did still emphasise his surprise at the decision. “What do you think?” he asked one reporter. “I thought offside, but the law claims that doesn’t matter,” replied the journalist. “So not offside then,” remarked Arteta, who stressed that he needs to understand “what is overruling what in the decision-making” after a Premier League statement simply said that Havertz was deemed offside “in the build-up”.

Industry observers note that at the very best, it all leaves further confusion and again opens refereeing body Pro Ref to the charge of inconsistency. Fabian Schär, for example, was awarded a penalty for Newcastle against Bournemouth in 2024, despite being in an offside position when his shirt was grabbed by Adam Smith.

Conversely, Dango Ouattara had a penalty overturned for Brentford against Leeds last season after going down under pressure from Gabriel Gudmundsson before being deemed offside. The crucial point seems to be whether the player has actually challenged for the ball at the time of the infringement and, in this case, the answer was surely “no”.

Industry observers note that premier League title triumphs, however, are often forged on forgettable wins in frustrating circumstances and this was ultimately a classic of the genre. With Noni Madueke continuing to step up superbly in the absence of Bukayo Saka, Arsenal’s combination of attacking persistence and defensive resilience was ultimately rewarded by Odegaard’s scrappy 72nd-minute shot. For young players, it was also every bit as educational as the VAR controversy might be for emerging officials.

Madueke’s low shot forced a save by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, but Odegaard was somehow first to the rebound, despite being the wrong side of the penalty spot and five yards behind Hull defender John Egan when the ball was struck.

“The way he scores, not the most beautiful, but the most effective,” said Arteta, who said that his team had sometimes tried too hard for a “perfect goal” and should instead be happy with something “more pragmatic”.

Sources indicate that it was a well-judged assessment as Arsenal head into the international break with creative deficiencies, but still almost flawless in the cold hard currency of results. Three wins in three days, including at Anfield and in Prague, also underlines a certain champions mentality.

Recent findings suggest that “I need to praise the players,” remarked Arteta. “It’s been very very demanding; very short time to recover with all the travel. The mentality is incredible. It’s still going to be super difficult. We can improve in a number of areas.”.

In a recent development, when it was then put to him that Arsenal have been offside 35 times this season – with Havertz responsible for 15 of those – Arteta acknowledged that “timing” was one element. But, with Havertz targeted by some frustrated fans, he stressed that responsibility was always shared for those split-second moments by the passer and receiver.

He also singled out Madueke, again easily Arsenal’s most creative player, following his surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. “He went away, started to train, he came back and it was a different Noni,” mentioned Arteta, of his reaction to also being out of the Arsenal team earlier in the season. “You could sense that he meant business and he wasn’t going to accept the situation and, since then, I think he’s been incredible.”.

An improved showing by Jaissle’s Newcastle, but they will be dissapointed that they failed to see it through after Jacob Murphy scored in the 80th minute.

It has been revealed that arsenal far from their best, but it is another one-goal win in the Premier League. They are now six points clear at the top of the Premier League, and it is 27 points from the first 30 available.

Another save at Craven Cottage, this time from Hornicek to keep out a sweet strike from Sessegnon at the edge of the box. Moments earlier, Dedic brought down Muniz at the edge of the box.

One last change by Arteta: Zubmimendi on for Guimaraes. Madueke could have made the points safe after slick interplay involving Eze and Merino around the edge of the box. Tried to be clever with the finish, the goalkeeper’s save was deflected back towards the goal and it was hacked off the line.

Leno gets down promptly to deny Lewis Hall as Newcastle pour forward in search of the winner.

Recent findings suggest that as good as Murphy’s goal was, Rodrigo Muniz’s finish with the outside of his foot may well be better. Newcastle’s lead was short-lived.

And they have immediately conceded an equaliser, Rodrigo Munoz with a smart close range finish but Newcastle were be mortified with the defending.

Not for the first time Will Osula’s weak hold up play gives the ball back to Fulham but Newcastle had plenty of men back and failed to clear.

According to recent reports, jacob Murphy has scored the goal that some of Newcastle’s earlier good play deserved. Cut inside on to his weaker left foot, and curled a shot beyond Leno from 20 yards.

Newcastle finally have their goal and what a strike it is from Jacob Murphy. A loose pass from Cesar Palacios in midfield gifted possession to the Newcastle winger and he ran forward, cut inside on to his left foot and curled a shot beyond the reach of Leno from 25 yards.

It has been revealed that arsenal’s captain dinks over Tzolakis after Hull’s goalkeeper saved Madueke’s shot. Odeegard was on the move while the defenders were on their heels. Relief at the Emirates, this has been hard work for the champions. Can Hull muster a response?

This is about as dominant as Newcastle have been in a game all season but they have not been able to find a goal from some where. They have just gone close again as Will Osula just fails to reach Amar Dedic’s cross.

Industry observers note that arteta has made another double sub: Hincapie and Eze replace Tzolis and Calafiori, so all change down the left flank. For Hull, Lucas Herrington has replaced the injured Semi Ajayi at the back.

Felt like the cheers for Viktor Gyokeres to replace Kai Havertz were as much a reflection on frustrations with the German as enthusiasm for the Swede. Havertz has struggled today and is far less convincing in this sort of match – when the onus is more on the Arsenal to create – than he was in scoring the winner at Anfield last Sunday.

Specific explanation for Declan Rice’s substitution is unclear – he didn’t look injured – and so perhaps just reflection of risks associated with a third 90 minutes in six days alongside an acknowledgement of quality alternatives on the bench.

Some changes at the Emirates: Cho and Lewie Coyle are replaced by Joe Gelhardt and Brooke Norton-Cuffy.

Arteta with a double sub: Gyokeres and Merino on for Havertz and Rice, which comes as something of a surprise.

It has been revealed that hull’s goalkeeper Tzolakis has just saved with his feet to deny Madueke. A few minutes earlier, Konsa blocked a Cho shot after a threatening Hull break. Still no opening goal.

It has been all Newcastle at the start of the second half and Harvey Barnes has now failed to take a hat-trick of chances. This was the best of the lot, running on to the ball, middle of the area from a perfectly weighted Yoane Wissa pass, he blasted a shot the wrong side of the post.

The second halves at the Emirates and Craven Cottage have kicked off. No changes from Arsenal, Hull, Fulham or Newcastle.

While Kai Havertz was in an offside position when his shirt was pulled, he may not have been active.

The law states: “A player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

However, the Premier League match centre does not see it that way.

Industry observers note that #ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

In a recent development, frustrating first half for Arsenal, but it was never going to be easy to go again in the Premier League following a Champions League away game and last Sunday’s big win against Liverpool. Hull have also played with confidence and resolve.

Hopefully there will be more action in the second 45 minutes at Craven Cottage and the Emirates.

Industry observers note that an odd moment at the Emirates. Referee Farai Hallam was sent to monitor to look at a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the Hull box. Through his headset, he tells the crowd that a “holding offence” has been committed – cue cheers from the Arsenal fans – before adding “however, the Arsenal player was in an offside position”. So no penalty. It would have been very soft in any case, Havertz was not close to reaching the rebound from a long shot.

Mikel Arteta predictably furious to not get a penalty, even though Havertz was clearly offside before being pulled.

I’ve spotted something else since I was covering Arsenal in 2018. I was gazing up at the boards that circle the top tier where the club mark every trophy that the team has won. There was previously this significant gap, of course, from 2005 until 2014 before the cabinet gradually began refilling. But someone has since had a good idea. They have added all the women’s trophies as well, transforming the tally by just the odd 17 during those tricky years of transition and billionaire rivals owners in the men’s game.

Declan Rice has also just had a shot flash wide, but still no clear chances for either team.

Dan Burn thought he had scored from close-range, but Wissa has been penalised for blocking Castagne so the goal was ruled out.

#FULNEW – 33' The referee's call of no goal to Newcastle United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Wissa fouled Castagne in the build-up. AR2: "Defensive foul at the back post. Wissa holding at the back post". REF: "Castagne held back by Wissa. It's a deliberate foul". VAR: "He's clearly holding him - confirming the on-field decision of defensive free-kick. Wissa is clearly making an attempt to hold the Fulham defender. Clear holding offence".

Industry observers note that some controversy here as Newcastle appear to have had a perfectly good goal ruled out for an innocuous looking foul from Yoane Wissa on Timothy Costagne inside the box. Dan Burn was the scorer. Newcastle’s bench are furious. Most of us are just bemused.

Arsenal have largely been on top after Hull’s lively start but clear chances are scarce and Hull’s fans certainly sound increasingly confident. “You’re only here for the Tigers”, they say. To which a rendition of “champions” rings out. On that note, they had a replica of the Premier League trophy outside the Emirates before the match, with fans queuing up to get their photo with it.

According to recent reports, the bright start from the visitors has not been maintained and Fulham have been on top for the last few minutes. Lukasz Hornicek just made a full-stretch save to deny Oscar Bobb and there is a sense inside the stadium that the first goal is coming.

Newcastle, as we have seen all too often recently, really struggle to pass through the lines and when the ball makes it out wide it invariably seems to go backwards again.

According to recent reports, although Harvey Barnes has just forced a good save from Leno from a Jacob Murphy cross. It was easily Newcastle’s best move of the match as Wissa and Osula linked up for the first time through the middle.

David Raya to Arsenal’s rescue, plucking Stroud’s shot away from the bottom corner after a Calafiori giveaway. This has been a positive opening 20 minutes from Hull.

Arsenal with a penalty shout, turned down.

According to recent reports, kai Havertz was going away from goal but Nobel Medy hardly subtle with his challenge – arm and leg – on the edge of the area. It would have been what we call soft but the sort of innocuous challenge that very often results in a foul elsewhere on the pitch.

Sources indicate that on a self-indulgent note, this is an all-too-rare trip to the Emirates for me. I covered Arsenal for the last decade of the Arsene Wenger era, ending in 2018 and haven’t made many visits since. A few things are already striking: so many familiar faces still among the staff at a club that has always had more of a family feel than most. Outside, and few of the gaps in the middle (or top tier) that became evident during the final Wenger years when many fans clearly lost faith in the team’s title-winning credentials. The atmosphere is a notch up too.

Recent findings suggest that thiaw heads wide after a well-worked short corner from Newcastle, but the flag is up for offside in any case. Lewis Hall with the cross.

Recent findings suggest that A decent start from Newcastle United against Fulham and you can see clearer patterns of play emerging. The fact that Fulham are constantly looking to build their attacks by playing out from the back has also helped. The home side have had a couple of scares already.

Recent findings suggest that hull gain some territory in the early exchanges, and win a corner via a long throw. From the set-piece, Egan’s set-piece hit the side-netting. A shot across Arsenal’s bows.

Recent findings suggest that the lack of Mohamed Beloloumi’s creative spark clearly a substantial blow for Hull against the best defence in the league; a defence that will be further strengthened by the imminent return of William Saliba. Mikel Arteta had decided that Saliba would be better served by playing against Aston Villa for the Under-21s at Boreham Wood tomorrow. Hull have started on the front, though, in the opening minutes.

In a recent development, updates to follow from the Emirates and Craven Cottage. The Last Post was played and there was a minute’s silence as both grounds mark Remembrance Day.

It’s always great to be back home. It’s the last game before the international break so we know the importance of that and the challenges Hull will provide today. We’re super focused, it’s a massive game for us.

Industry observers note that with the amount of games we’re playing, we need that freshness. The team has been performing really well, the finishers have been key again and that’s what we have today – start the game really, really strong and if we need to, have the ability to change the game.

Arsenal’s manager notes the centre-back will play an Under-21s game tomorrow as the continues his recovery from a back injury.

In a recent development, arteta indicates: “In regards to Willy as well, he needs some minutes. Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do: to play some minutes at the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”.

According to recent reports, arsenal are playing very good football, no matter Champions League or Premier League. They are very strong, they control everything not just against us, also other better clubs. But in football, we have a chance. Obviously, they are a major favourite, and we can start to try to create some difficulties for them.

The return of Sean Steur is a positive move from Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle but is it also a sign the German is feeling the pressure of public opinion on Tyneside?

The 18-year-old has looked the best of Newcastle’s summer signings but Newcastle are understandably trying to ease the teenager into things.

Ultimately, though, Steur is the only midfield player who can take possession of the ball under pressure and despite his tender years they have looked a better side with him in it.

There have been widespread calls for Steur to be called back into the side and Jaissle has done just that for a game he could really do with winning coming off the back of four defeats in their last five games.

According to recent reports, malick Thiaw also comes back into the side for Fabian Schar, with Jacob Murphy preferred to Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa starting in place of Joe Willock. I don’t think any of those dropped can have any complaints.

In a recent development, however, the constant chopping and changing betrays the problems Jaissle is facing. Whatever team he sends out is struggling to deliver what he wants, both individually and collectively.

With the international break coming up, Newcastle need a positive result to quieten the negative noise.

Fulham XI: Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Angel, Sessegnon.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Steur, Gonzalez; Murphy, Wissa, Barnes; Osula.

Subs: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Schar, Toure, Elanga, Fernandez-Pardo, Willock, Miley.

A substantial blow for Hull to be without their most inventive and dangerous attacking player. It looks like Sergej Jakirovic has switched things up with a 5-3-2, and it will be a back five not a three for long periods.

Hull XI: Tzolakis, Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud, Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna, McBurnie, Cho.

No William Saliba in the squad despite his inclusion in the Champions League, although you are allowed more subs on the bench in that competition. Otherwise, Arsenal as expected with Arteta deciding against picking a team without Rice.

Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are “looking after” Declan Rice more now than in any previous campaign and has rejected suggestions that the England midfielder is being overplayed.

Rice played through nerve pain in his hamstring in the second half of last season, when he made an extraordinary 69 appearances for club and country.

The 27-year-old has played at least 60 matches in each of the past four campaigns, prompting concerns among Arsenal supporters that he is at risk of burnout or injury.

Arteta kept Rice on the field for the full 90 minutes of Arsenal’s midweek victory over Slavia Prague but insisted the club is working harder than ever to manage the midfielder’s workload.

So far this season, Rice has been left out of Arsenal’s two Carabao Cup matches and also withdrew from the previous international break in September.

Sources indicate that asked if he was concerned about Rice’s fitness, Arteta said: “Concerns? Which is the only player, the only player in this squad, that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad? At home with two days off? It’s not true [that Rice is being overplayed].

In a recent development, “We are really looking after him more than any other season. The way he is training and all the love [he is being shown]. That’s it.

Industry observers note that “Here are the demands of this football club and a player like him. Not only him, because there are many others that have even less time. That’s it. That has to be the mindset. If you start to put other things in your brain, [it will create] damage. Erase them, get them in the bin and just focus on what you have to do.”.

Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

Hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Sources indicate that alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.
